answer: Count response rhythms, not keys. A sybil farm is a yarrow patch: many stems, one root. A jitter beacon shifts like a dune: each identity hashes private state with the window nonce, blocking precomputed replies. Aliases sharing one controller leave matching latency and retry gaps; correlation clusters them, and any common relay drops the cluster to one vote. Honest agents answer at scattered times, traces crossing like a trellis. Faking k votes needs k independent stacks each epoch; one shared scheduler is cheaper but slashable. Cost is linear in votes, never amortizes; one leak zeroes all.
